Overnight, careful habits for gate queues
This page shows new staff what to do first
Companion Animal Travel Desk work is about calm checks, clear handoffs, and keeping each pet moving safely through the skyport. It matters because passengers trust us with animals that may be nervous, tired, or eager to get home, and because the rest of the airport team needs our notes to be quick and accurate. A brisk start helps everyone, especially when the gate area gets busy and a small mistake can ripple through the whole trip.

When you arrive, look over the day’s animal cases and the paperwork beside them. Check that the traveler name on the booking matches the animal details, and make sure the carrier is in good shape, closed properly, and labeled the way local rules require. If anything looks off, pause and call the senior coordinator before you move the booking ahead. Never guess, never rush, and never promise that a pet will travel until the checks are done.

Use plain language with passengers. Tell them what you are doing, what they need to keep ready, and where they should stand while you sort the next step. Keep your tone kind but steady. If a traveler arrives worried about Trixie, for example, give brief reassurance and then focus on the facts: the carrier, the documents, and the handoff to the next crew member. The goal is not a long talk. The goal is a safe trip and a smooth queue.

At the desk, write notes that another teammate can read at a glance. Note special handling needs, feeding reminders, and any sign of stress that matters for the journey. Use the same clean routine each time so the crew can trust your work. If you spot a conflict between the booking and the animal record, stop the process and bring in the supervisor right away.

Aurelia Skyways moves people and pets between skyports, so our desk has to stay sharp, steady, and easy to understand. Remember to check first, speak clearly, and protect safety before speed. Companion Animal Travel Desk
